verified_positive_evidence: Campaign run() evaluates candidates only through development inner-CV; the manifest states holdout_policy='never evaluated by run(); explicit certify command only'.
Each trial starts from the current frozen best source tree in a non-overwritten workspace, with source_sha256 and append-only ledger records.
certify() rechecks the exact best source tree hash before holdout evaluation and writes a certificate bound to trial_id and source_sha256.
The public test explicitly runs one trial, resumes to a second trial, verifies no holdout_certification exists during run(), then invokes certify().
The method contract states an outer fold is sealed, candidates are selected using inner K-fold CV, exact source tree/hash are frozen, and one explicit certification scores the outer fold.
The public paper artifact claims all retained trials, frozen winners and certification scores are released with hash-verification scripts.
critical_gaps: There is no separate CERTIFY surface between adaptive development selection and OUTER; the holdout itself is the certification result, so this is a three-surface rather than LOGOS four-surface design.

certify() executes evaluator.holdout(workspace) before checking whether holdout_certification.json already exists, so repeated certify calls re-query the outer holdout even when a prior certificate is present.
The public test itself calls certify() twice; it verifies deterministic certificate identity but therefore also exercises repeated outer evaluation rather than enforcing one-shot consumption.
run() does not check that holdout certification has occurred and does not close/finalize the campaign after certification; executable code therefore does not prevent run-after-certify continuation.

holdout_certification.json is written with ordinary write_text after the evaluator returns. A crash after outer evaluation but before durable write can consume the outer surface without a local certificate, allowing retry to re-query it.
No candidate-local anytime-valid gate or cross-candidate statistical spending governs development selection.

design_update.rule: A separate certification command is not sufficient to make OUTER a terminal lockbox. The evaluator consumption must be monotone and terminal in the campaign state machine.
outer_lockbox_contract: first outer query requires immutable selected artifact identity and explicit terminal transition intent
logical_outer_query_id and query budget are durably prepared before evaluator dispatch
outer result is consumed at most once logically; retry must reconcile the same logical query rather than create a fresh evaluation
after first outer result becomes observable, search/tune/promotion/rollback/router/stopping state cannot be reopened using that result
repeated certify is either a pure read of the stored certificate or is rejected, never a new evaluator call
campaign state records a monotone transition such as SEARCH_OPEN -> FROZEN -> CERTIFYING -> CERTIFIED/CLOSED

exact_next_action: Search for a public self-improvement system that enforces a monotone terminal outer-lockbox state machine in code/tests, preferably with durable pre-dispatch logical query accounting. Combine this with the still-missing LOGOS-like candidate-local anytime-valid CERTIFY and cross-candidate durable spending. Specifically look for implementations where repeated certify is cache/read-only or rejected, run-after-certify is impossible, and crash between outer dispatch/result persistence cannot create a second logical outer query.
